Class LinkAnnotator

java.lang.Object
org.casserole.format.LinkAnnotator
public final class LinkAnnotator extends Object
The LinkAnnotator type marks http and https addresses so a capable terminal can open them. Each accepted address is wrapped in a purple SGR sequence and an OSC 8 sequence. SGR is the select-graphic-rendition sequence that sets terminal color. OSC 8 is the terminal sequence that attaches a link to displayed text. Text that already contains an OSC 8 opener is left unchanged. An address that contains a carriage return or a line feed is left as ordinary text. The type has no instances.

  • Method Details

    • annotate

      public static String annotate(String text)
      The annotate method marks web addresses in text that already uses carriage-return line feeds. A null or empty text returns the empty string. If the text already contains the OSC 8 opener, the method returns the text unchanged. indexOfHttp(String, int) finds the next http:// or https://. extendUrl(String, int) takes the run, and trimTrailingPunct(String) drops a trailing period, comma, semicolon, or closing bracket. If that address contains a carriage return or a line feed, or if it is shorter than eight characters, the original run is copied without a link. Otherwise the method writes purple, the OSC 8 opener, the address, BEL, the visible address, a closing OSC 8, and the reset sequence. Punctuation removed from the address is written after the link.
      Parameters:
      text - The canvas text, already normalized to carriage-return line feeds.
      Returns:
      The text with accepted addresses marked.

    • indexOfHttp

      private static int indexOfHttp(String text, int from)
      The indexOfHttp method finds the next web address prefix. The method searches for https:// and for http:// from from. If only one prefix is present, that index is returned. If both are present, the earlier index is returned. If neither is present, the method returns -1.
      Parameters:
      text - The text being scanned.
      from - The index at which the scan starts.
      Returns:
      The index of http:// or https://, or -1.

    • extendUrl

      private static int extendUrl(String text, int start)
      The extendUrl method finds the end of one address run. The run stops before a character whose code is 32 or less. The run also stops before <, >, a quotation mark, an apostrophe, or ).
      Parameters:
      text - The text being scanned.
      start - The index where the address starts.
      Returns:
      The exclusive end index of the run.

    • trimTrailingPunct

      private static String trimTrailingPunct(String url)
      The trimTrailingPunct method removes trailing punctuation from an address. A trailing ., ,, ;, or ] is removed, and the removal repeats. Any other ending is kept.
      Parameters:
      url - The raw address run.
      Returns:
      The address without that trailing punctuation.
